body: claimed: issue-worker-high (Opus 5.5) · 2026-11-13 09:54 UTC · worktree/branch issue/796-tormach-wrapped-a (not created yet) · plan: check whether wrapped-A posting can ship without the held rotary-feed PRs and the open PathPilot questions

Blocked. No code written and no branch pushed.

Why this can't be done safely yet:

1. **Rotary feed depends on held PR #951 (#885).** A simultaneous XYZA feed has to hold the microARC 4's stated A rate. #951 adds the shared rule that does this (`crates/post/src/post/rotary_cap.rs`: `rotaryRate` / `rotaryFeedCap` / `rotaryFeed`). Its body says `tormach.cps` needs no cap only because it refuses an A that changes inside an operation. #951 is unmerged (needs-rework), and #952 is stacked on it. A second copy of that rule in `tormach.cps` would duplicate it and conflict with it. Posting wrapped A with no rate cap would let F carry A past its rate, and that output is not safe.
2. **The two open questions on this issue are still unanswered.** One is whether PathPilot wraps A (rollover) or treats it as linear degrees. The other is how it reads F on a combined XYZA move (G94 or G93). The public LinuxCNC docs leave rollover to each machine's configuration (the wrapped-rotary joint setting), and the Tormach guides don't say which one the microARC 4 uses. The issue's own Work list says to settle both in the PathPilot Hub and on the 770MX first, and "Done means" includes a cut on the hardware. An agent can do neither.

Until then, the safe state on main stays as it is: `tormach.cps` refuses by name an A that changes inside an operation ("simultaneous 4-axis motion ... not confirmed on PathPilot"), and `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_is_refused_by_name` pins that.

Unblocks when: #951 merges (so the shared rate rule exists), and the rollover and feed-mode answers are recorded here from a Hub run or the machine.
